title: Korea Clears Safety Rules to Put 20 Humanoid Robots on Factory Floors
key_facts: South Korea's Ministry of Trade and Industry held the sixth 2026 meeting of its Industrial Convergence Regulatory Sandbox Committee on 13 Oct 2026 and granted a demonstration exemption to robot maker Robros.

Under the pilot, 20 of Robros' AI-powered bipedal humanoids will work at Nepes (semiconductor back-end packaging), Sungwoo Hitech (auto body parts), HD Hyundai Samho (shipbuilding scaffolding) and Delivery Lab (refrigerated logistics packaging).
Existing rules treated industrial robots as stationary equipment and required safety fences and other barriers to separate human and robot work areas.
The exemption is conditional on risk assessments and safety measures, and the data gathered will be used to draw up future safety standards.
In August the government unveiled a plan to invest a cumulative 2.3 trillion won ($1.6 billion) in the humanoid sector by 2030 and to buy 1,080 domestically made humanoids.
Trade and Industry Minister Kim Jung-kwan said regulation struggles to keep up with AI and institutional bottlenecks must be removed quickly.
quote_evidence: The committee granted a demonstration exemption to Robros, a domestic robot maker developing bipedal humanoids, for its project deploying humanoid robots at semiconductor, automotive, shipbuilding and logistics sites.
Under the pilot, 20 of Robros' AI-powered bipedal humanoids will be deployed at Nepes, Sungwoo Hitech, HD Hyundai Samho and Delivery Lab.
Before the exemption, existing rules treated industrial robots as stationary equipment and required safety fences and other barriers to separate human and robot work areas.
why_it_matters_hint: Korea is testing walking robots beside workers in four industries and will use the data to write safety rules.
notes: Seoul Economic Daily article, AI-translated from Korean (as the page states). Reported from government officials; the robots are to be deployed, not yet working.
